To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relationship between shareholder gender (i.e., female ownership) and earnings management (in terms of the magnitude of abnormal discretionary accruals) is not linear but quadratic and that the practice of earnings management is not opposed by the presence of a female shareholder but rather by the presence of shareholder gender heterogeneity.

the relationship between shareholder gender (i.e. the presence of women in the ownership structure) and the magnitude of earnings management is not linear (i.e. it is not a simple matter of more or less women in the ownership group) but quadratic (i.e. there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between the number of women in the group and the magnitude of discretionary accruals).
the relationship between shareholder gender diversity and earnings management is not linear, but quadratic.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the gender of shareholders is a relevant factor in the decision to manage earnings and that gender diversity in the ownership structure of a company is a key element in reducing earnings manipulation.
female shareholders are not more likely to be engaged in earnings management, as long as there is no gender heterogeneity in ownership.
the presence of women in a firm's ownership structure is not a panacea to reduce the magnitude of discretionary accruals.
